home.text: I design interfaces backed by real user research, and understand the technical side that makes them realistically implementable. This portfolio was designed and developed by me — proof that research, design and development can work together end-to-end.

about.title: From user research to production code —
about.title-accent: how I bridge design and development.
about.text: Since the beginning of my journey I've combined curiosity, creativity and technology. I start every project with research — interviews, surveys, competitive analysis — to validate what the real problem is before designing a solution. My background in computer science then lets me translate those decisions into interfaces that are not only effective for users, but realistically implementable for developers — sometimes building them myself. This approach reduces misunderstandings between research, design and development, and makes the production process smoother: ideas don't remain just concepts, they become concrete, validated, and achievable solutions.

fisiogest-sr-title: FisioGest — Clinic Management Platform for Physiotherapists
fisiogest-sr-role: UX/UI Designer & Front-end Developer. Masamune Academy, one-month Agile Scrum sprint, team of four. Davide's first paid professional project.
fisiogest-sr-summary: FisioGest is management software for physiotherapy practices. Davide followed the entire project end to end, from user research to front-end code, within a four-person Agile Scrum team over one month at Masamune Academy.
fisiogest-sr-process: Research began with interviews with physiotherapists and osteopaths. Interview recordings and transcripts were analyzed with AI support (NotebookLM) to identify recurring patterns, which were synthesized into a pain map that guided the design decisions.
fisiogest-sr-workflow-1: Augmented Research (NotebookLM & Survey): strategic surveys generated with AI support; interviews transformed into structured datasets with objective metrics.
fisiogest-sr-workflow-2: Design Ops & Bridge (MCP + Claude Code): Design Tokens defined in Figma were interpreted by Claude Code, via the Model Context Protocol, to generate the Design System scaffolding.
fisiogest-sr-workflow-3: Engineering & Refinement (Tailwind CSS + Shadcn UI): production-ready React components, built Mobile-First with Desktop consistency.
fisiogest-sr-designsystem: Design System v1.0, built on Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI with the Inter typeface, meeting WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. It is Mobile-First with a minimum 44px touch target, responsive from 375 to 1440 pixels, and includes color tokens, an 8px-based typography scale, and stateful components such as buttons, badges, and inputs.
fisiogest-sr-deliverables: User research, personas, user flows, wireframes, a complete Design System, UI kit, prototypes, and front-end development.
fisiogest-alt-01: FisioGest hero screen: logo, tagline 'Simplifying Daily Operations for Physiotherapists', a weekly schedule view listing patients and treatments, and a phone mockup of the patient search screen.
fisiogest-alt-02: Product overview slide: FisioGest Product Design summary covering project type (SaaS for physiotherapy clinics), the challenge of digitizing analog workflows, and the target audience of freelancers and small clinics managing 10 to 40 patients weekly.
fisiogest-alt-03: The AI-Driven Production Loop: three phases — Augmented Research with NotebookLM and AI-generated surveys, Design Ops & Bridge translating Figma tokens into code via MCP and Claude Code, and Engineering & Refinement with Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI — with code snippets and stats on audio analyzed, design tokens and components produced.
fisiogest-alt-04: Problem statement slide: four pain points — an hour lost daily juggling WhatsApp, Excel and manual reminders, 2-3 weekly no-shows, the mental stress of remembering everything, and clinics describing their methods as 'stone age'.
fisiogest-alt-05: Human-Centered Design Process: four phases — Discovery, Define, Ideation and Validation — each listing the research and design activities carried out.
fisiogest-alt-06: From Hypotheses to User Stories: three cards showing hypotheses on booking speed, no-show anxiety and visual pain tracking, each validated against research data and a supporting user quote.
fisiogest-alt-07: Design Sprint Cycles: three iteration stages — The Agenda, Patient Card and Integrated System — summarizing how each part of the product evolved.
fisiogest-alt-08: Information architecture diagram: from the homepage and login/register flow into the web app's three core modules — Schedule, Patients and Incomes — with their sub-features.
fisiogest-alt-09: User journey map for booking an appointment during a phone call, broken into four timed steps: start and search slots, patient selection, visit setup, and success with automatic recall.
fisiogest-alt-10: Continuation of the journey map: emotions and pain points at each step, paired with the resulting design opportunities and impact metrics, including a 62% drop in double-booking errors and 100% of WhatsApp recalls activated.
fisiogest-alt-11: Impact and success metrics: an 83% cut in daily paperwork, under-30-second appointment booking, zero lost sessions from no-shows, 100% real-time revenue visibility, and a single unified hub replacing paper archives.
fisiogest-alt-12: Mobile-first section with a phone mockup of the FisioGest onboarding screen: 'Forget the paperwork. Focus on your patients.'
fisiogest-alt-13: Smart scheduling flow across three phone mockups: a scannable appointment card list, progressive disclosure of notes and quick actions, and immediate visual feedback when a reminder is sent.
fisiogest-alt-14: Desktop mockup of the Schedule module's weekly table view, with callouts on the weekly overview, administrative management and slot optimization features.
fisiogest-alt-15: Patient management section: phone mockups of the searchable patient list and a five-tab patient profile with direct call and WhatsApp actions.
fisiogest-alt-16: Phone mockup of pain-score and improvement KPIs with a trend chart, next to a desktop mockup of the therapeutic pathway timeline organized by body area.
fisiogest-alt-17: Income control section: three phone mockups of the Revenue module showing payment status monitoring, bulk 'mark as paid' actions, and the payment method selection screen.
fisiogest-alt-18: Revenue module on desktop: a dashboard summary of confirmed and no-show appointments, the daily collected amount and patients seen, and a payment tracking table with per-visit status and a bulk 'Mark as Paid' action.
fisiogest-alt-19: Design System & Scalability section opening with 'A Redesign of Traditional Pain Maps': a Cervical Pain body diagram highlighting the treated area in red and linking the pain cause with a connecting line, a list of the points involved, and three guiding principles — one highlighted area per treatment pathway, linking pain to its cause, and a low-to-high color intensity system.
fisiogest-alt-20: Specialized assessment tools: anatomical pain maps for the foot (hallux, metatarsus) and spine (S5, sacral apex), followed by the Design System & Scalability overview listing the Tailwind CSS v4, Shadcn UI, Inter, WCAG 2.1 AA, Mobile-First and Design Tokens foundations.
fisiogest-alt-21: Design system foundations: color tokens for brand, neutral and status colors with their hex values; button states (primary, secondary outlined, ghost) across default, hover, loading and disabled; status badges and priority pills built for WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility; and input field states including a search bar, default text fields and an error state.
fisiogest-alt-22: Design system documentation: typography specs, and navigation components (tab bar, mobile bottom bar, desktop sidebar) with their design tokens, closing with a 'Thanks for reading' slide.
lume-sr-title: Lume — Smart Energy Bill Management App
lume-sr-role: Lead UX/UI Designer. Boolean × IMILLE, five-month project, team of three.
lume-sr-summary: Lume is an app that helps people understand and manage their energy bills. This was Davide's first UX/UI project, with research conducted and synthesized entirely by hand.
lume-sr-method: The research combined a survey of 77 users aged 30 to 55 with 8 in-depth one-to-one qualitative interviews, alongside competitor benchmarking and usability testing.
lume-sr-insight: Asked what they would change about their bill experience, users pointed to clarity and simplicity (25%), better graphics and UX (16.1%), and cost detail (6.5%), with 22.6% giving other, spontaneous responses.
lume-sr-solution: The resulting design includes a real-time consumption dashboard, gamified saving challenges, educational tooltips, and Lumy, the brand's mascot.
lume-sr-accessibility: The Design System complies with WCAG 2.1 AA, covering color contrast, touch target size, and visible focus states.
lume-sr-deliverables: User flows, information architecture, wireframes, prototypes, UI, and a complete Design System.
lume-alt-01: Lume app hero screens: energy dashboard, bill details with cost breakdown, and the Lumy energy coach's weekly actions, alongside the project overview, goals and challenges.
lume-alt-02: Onboarding screen introducing Lumy, the app's mascot, with a warm welcome message.
lume-alt-03: Phone mockups of the bill details, consumption dashboard and profile screens, next to the six-phase project roadmap: Discovery & Strategy, UX Research, Ideation & Lead UX, Validation, UI & Content, Prototype & Handoff.
lume-alt-04: Three app screens showing the electricity and gas overview, the real-time consumption dashboard, and Lumy's weekly actions.
lume-alt-05: Five user research insight cards on bill anxiety and complexity, alongside the key insight panel and survey results on what users would change about their bill experience.
lume-alt-06: Utility switch screen: a single toggle to move between electricity and gas without losing context.
lume-alt-07: Close-up of the live consumption dashboard reading 124 kWh.
lume-alt-08: Lumy the mascot celebrating next to the weekly saving challenges screen.
lume-alt-09: Gamification badges (The Champion, Tree Hugger, CoinHero, Night Owl) and the Lumy coach screen, shown alongside photos of users interacting with the app.
lume-alt-10: Latest bill screen showing payment status, daytime versus nighttime usage split, and the billed amount.
lume-alt-11: Design System components, Lumy's mascot expressions, the Lume brand identity, color palette, typography, and the project's landing page and team credits.
clinicsoul-sr-title: ClinicSoul — UX Redesign of a Clinical Management System
clinicsoul-sr-role: UX Researcher & Designer. Masamune Academy, one-month Agile Scrum sprint, team of ten.
clinicsoul-sr-summary: ClinicSoul is the UX redesign of a clinical management system that had been built almost entirely with AI and unvalidated internal assumptions.
clinicsoul-sr-discovery: The research uncovered that the AI had hallucinated entire workflows misaligned with how doctors, receptionists, and clinic owners actually work.
clinicsoul-sr-method: The team ran four semi-structured interviews and a survey with 23 participants. Interviews and recordings were analyzed with AI support (NotebookLM) to identify recurring themes.
clinicsoul-sr-deliverables: A complete restructuring of the information architecture around five operational pillars — Calendar, Patient Management, Clinic Management, Accounting, and Settings — plus a benchmark against five competitors: XDENT, Alfadocs, Cliniko, MioDottore, and Doctolib.
clinicsoul-alt-01: ClinicSoul hero slide: logo, 'UX Redesign Case Study' tagline about improving an AI-shaped clinical platform through UX research, and a dashboard screenshot with appointments and revenue metrics.
clinicsoul-alt-02: Slide on the project's starting point: the platform was shaped by AI-assisted ideation without a UX research process, listing the resulting challenges, next to a phone screen for selecting a clinical specialty.
clinicsoul-alt-03: Goals and outcomes slide: five cards covering validating assumptions, uncovering real user needs, clinical flow alignment, feature reduction, and future foundation, each paired with its outcome.
clinicsoul-alt-04: Research methods slide: research objectives across clinical, administrative and business needs, the methods used (semi-structured interviews, Figma prototype walkthroughs, a survey), and the sample size of 23 survey participants and 4 in-depth interviews.
clinicsoul-alt-05: User persona 'Lorenzo Rossi', a 40-year-old nutritionist, with his needs, goals and pain points.
clinicsoul-alt-06: Empathy map for the Lorenzo Rossi persona, covering what he says, does, thinks and feels.
clinicsoul-alt-07: Patient journey map from start to end of day, showing feelings, actions, thoughts and improvement opportunities across consultations, administrative tasks and patient communication.
clinicsoul-alt-08: User persona 'Elena Ferraro', a 51-year-old dental assistant and receptionist, with her needs, goals and pain points.
clinicsoul-alt-09: Empathy map for the Elena Ferraro persona, covering what she says, does, thinks and feels.
clinicsoul-alt-10: Second journey map from start to end of day, covering appointment management, patient support and administrative tasks with associated feelings and improvement opportunities.
clinicsoul-alt-11: Section intro slide: 'What did we learn from our users?', introducing the insights grouped into three main categories.
clinicsoul-alt-12: Direct quotes from interview participants grouped into three themes: naming and visual clarity, flexibility and adaptability, and system guidance and support.
clinicsoul-alt-13: Four insights on naming and visual clarity: terminology consistency, color as operational code, information hierarchy, and moving from a 'startup' look to a 'trust' look.
clinicsoul-alt-14: Four insights on flexibility and adaptability: different roles need different priorities, data legal integrity, flexibility as a top priority, and digital acquisition.
clinicsoul-alt-15: Four insights on system guidance and support: smart filters, preserving the human touch, AI as assistant not pilot, and availability visualization.
clinicsoul-alt-16: Benchmark matrix comparing ClinicSoul against five competitors — XDENT, Alfadocs, Cliniko, MioDottore and Doctolib — across first impression, ease of learning, feature organization, automation and innovation, and operational efficiency.
clinicsoul-alt-17: Information architecture diagram showing the redesigned user flow around five pillars: Calendar, Patient Management, Clinic Management, Accounting and Settings.
clinicsoul-alt-18: Closing slide: project conclusion on moving from assumptions to evidence-based decisions, followed by a 'Thank you for reading' slide with the ClinicSoul mascot.
brunocambiaso-meta-desc: UI design case study for Bruno Cambiaso, a minimal portfolio site for a painter, built with Next.js, Sanity CMS and Tailwind CSS.
brunocambiaso-description: A minimal, essential portfolio for a painter exhibiting oil, acrylic and mixed-media work — designed so the artwork stays the protagonist, not the interface. Quiet typography, generous white space, and a UI that stays almost entirely out of the way, letting color come from the paintings themselves.
